title: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer — RadLab Evidence Crosswalk

evidence_policy.primary_direct: The source directly provides measured radiation observations relevant to the mission's learning objective.
evidence_policy.supporting: The source provides real research context, but does not directly validate the simulated engineering outcome.
evidence_policy.background_only: Contextual reference only; it is not evidence for the simulated operational outcome.
evidence_policy.not_supported: No direct dataset relationship is claimed.

sources.title: A Trip Through a Space Storm

research_reference.title: Space radiation measurements during the Artemis I lunar mission

limitations: The event JSON contains instrument peak summaries, not individual time-series rows.
Underlying readings are retained in the separate raw CSV files.
Artemis I was an uncrewed test flight.
Absorbed dose rate is not dose equivalent rate.
Different instruments and sensor positions are not interchangeable.

sources.title: Artemis I Outer Earth Radiation Belt Passage

research_reference.title: Space radiation measurements during the Artemis I lunar mission

limitations: Artemis I was an uncrewed test flight.
Absorbed dose rate is not dose equivalent rate.
The outer-belt interval is an electron-rich radiation-belt passage.
Do not interpret this event as a solar energetic particle event.
The event's contribution to cumulative mission dose was small in the published study.

sources.title: Artemis I lunar flyby radiation measurements

research_reference.title: Space radiation measurements during the Artemis I lunar mission

limitations: Artemis I was an uncrewed test flight.
Absorbed dose rate is not dose equivalent rate.
Windowed averages in this dataset are not the same calculation as the published approximately one-third GCR reduction.
The published lunar shielding interpretation concerns part of the incoming galactic cosmic-ray field.
Do not claim the Moon blocks all space radiation.

mappings.rationale: Archived Orion instrument measurements provide real absorbed-dose-rate observations across an inner-belt passage, an outer-belt passage and two lunar flyby periods.
mappings.implementation_note: Extend the existing ISS-focused activity with a separate historical Artemis I dataset view. Clearly label the spacecraft, instrument, sensor location, date and uncrewed mission status.
limitations: Do not present Artemis I readings as astronaut exposure.
Do not label Orion readings as ISS, lunar-surface or Mars-surface readings.
Do not treat absorbed dose rate and dose equivalent rate as interchangeable.
Keep each instrument's readings and sensor position distinct.

mappings.rationale: The datasets allow learners to inspect real time-series measurements, compare time windows and understand why instrument, position and measurement definition matter.
mappings.implementation_note: Use separate charts or clearly labelled series. Compare like-for-like units and identify the sensor before asking which chart is higher.
limitations: Do not compare different instruments as if they were identical sensors.
Do not compare values with different units as if they were the same quantity.
The inner-belt event file contains peak summaries; its raw CSV files hold the underlying measurements.

mappings.rationale: Real spacecraft radiation observations provide context for discussing why spacecraft layout and shielding matter.
mappings.implementation_note: Keep shelter construction, material choices and protection outcomes explicitly simulated or conceptual unless a separately validated shielding model is added.
limitations: These datasets do not validate a Moon or Mars shelter design.
Do not infer shielding effectiveness solely from differences between sensors at different locations.
Do not present game protection percentages as measured NASA results.

not_supported_examples.reason: The Artemis event files describe radiation-belt passages. They do not establish that the observations are measurements of a specific solar energetic particle event. Use a matching DONKI SEP record for the event activity.
These historical RadLab measurements are not solar-flare or CME event records and are not a live space-weather alert feed. Retain the relevant DONKI sources for these missions.

simulation_boundary: Artemis I was uncrewed; none of these measurements represent astronaut exposure.
The measured quantity in these event datasets is absorbed dose rate in microGy/hour.
Do not infer dose equivalent rate in microSv/hour without a justified radiation weighting or conversion model.
Do not present these spacecraft measurements as measurements at a fictional lunar or Martian base.
Shelter designs, material performance and game protection outcomes remain simulated unless separately validated.
The published approximately one-third GCR reduction during lunar flybys is a research finding and is not the same as the windowed percentage changes calculated in this dataset.
Keep raw telemetry, derived summaries, published research interpretation and game simulation as separate evidence layers.
